Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Objective 2 Setup 3 On Your Turn 3.1 Note 3.2 Actions 3.2.1 Satisfy Customers 3.2.2 Go back to the Kitchen 3.2.3 Dump your Tray 4 Winning 5 Variants 5.1 Poaching and Blocking 5.2 Opening a Buffet 5.3 Expansions 6 Solo 6.1 Objective 6.2 How to Play 6.3 The Kitchen is Closing 6.4 How to Win 6.5 Remaining Guests Rank Objective Satisfy customers with your desserts to collect enough customers and win the game. Setup Each player starts with 3 desserts of their own (not visible to other players). 3 guests visible to all players are at the centre of the table (top of the screen on BGA). On Your Turn Draw a dessert and draw a guest to the centre of the table Note If the last dessert has been drawn, then the discard pile will be reshuffled into the draw pile. If the last guest has been drawn, then all cards below the top of the discard pile will be reshuffled into the draw pile. Actions Choose 1 of 3 available actions: Satisfy Customers Discard dessert cards to fully satisfy all of a guest's cravings without giving them anything that they refuse, then move that guest in front of you. If you use their favourite, draw a dessert. You can serve at most 2 customers. To serve a guest: Select one or more desserts that fully satisfy the customer and click on the cards. Select the customer you are serving. Select serve guest . Go back to the Kitchen Draw a dessert. Dump your Tray Discard any number of desserts and draw the same number back. If there are any guests with duplicate suits at the end of a turn, remove guests until there is at most 1 of each suit remaining. The most recently departed guest can also be served. Winning You win if you have three guests of the same suit or five guests of all different suits. If no one achieved victory when all guests are served (including the face-up guests, not just an empty draw pile), everyone scores 1 for each guest and 1 for each pair of matching guest. The highest score wins. In case of a tie, whoever has the most desserts remaining wins. Variants Poaching and Blocking Once per turn, you may attempt to poach (steal) a customer from another player. You may attempt to poach a customer by satisfying them. That player can block by re-satisfying them. If you poach with a favourite, it can only be blocked by another favourite. If you are blocked, you take back all the cards you played. A player whose guest is stolen draws a dessert. If any favourites are served, the players draw a card for each favourite they played. Opening a Buffet This is a fourth turn option. To open a buffet, you need to play 4 single-flavoured cards. If a buffet is opened, all opponents need to put a guest of their choice back to the middle. Then, you draw 3 cards and can serve a guest. Expansions The expansions are Just Coffee and Better with Bacon. They provide 6 new desserts and 4 new customers each. Each pack also introduces a new flavor and a new suit. To select these expansions, you must have a premium membership. Solo Objective Satisfy as many Guests as possible before the Desserts are all gone! How to Play Follow the standard rules for the way a Guest is satisfied by discarding one or more Dessert cards. When you satisfy someone, add a new Guest to the hungry lineup. You also draw an extra Dessert card immediately if you give a Guest their Favorite thing. Discarding Desserts : When you’ve satisfied as many of the Guests as you can (or wish to) with the Dessert cards you have, discard 3 (or all of your cards if you have 3 or fewer). After discarding, draw again until you have 5 Dessert cards. The Kitchen is Closing When the Dessert card draw pile is almost gone, you will get all of the remaining Dessert cards into your hand at once. community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] The game consists of draw a card, match the symbols = good, if not bad, draw more cards.  Occasionally your opponent can snatch guests you have already served.  Art was appropriate.

[Rating: 1/10] First, I start with a game.  Then I take away interactions, player agency and interesting choices.  What's left?  Just Desserts.

[Rating: 2/10] Neither the best (Chrononauts) nor the worst (Fluxx) of the chaotic Andrew Looney card games, this is nonetheless in a similar vein: easy to explain, chaotic, and very tactical (to be generous as it may lack both strategy and tactics in any significant quantity).  The enjoyment is perhaps more in the incredible range of fancy desserts featured on the cards than it is in the gameplay.

[Rating: 2/10] This...isn't even a game. There's no decisions to be made. Draw a card, see if you match symbols. No? Turn over. Yes? Do the thing. Rinse, repeat.

[Rating: 2/10] FIRST IMPRESSION:  Meh, it was annoying to keep getting my stuff purloined by my opponent. Makes sense for my opponent to do so but there was too much luck and annoying theft that left me cold. Only reason I played was part of a BGA Open tournament that did not go well for me! :-) I hopefully won't have to play this one ever again.

[Rating: 2/10] Major luckfest that ends up just dragging. Fun art, I guess, but that can't save how this game is just hope you draw the right card. If everyone on the board wants a fruity desert and you don't draw fruit then you don't play. It also means when you can do something on your turn, it isn't interesting or even really a decision, you just play the cards that you can play. Pointless.

[Rating: 2/10] These games make me think if I even like card games or just hate them. So what are we doing here? Get a card or buy a customer or rebuy a customer from the opponent. So we wait if we get the right ressources or the right customer appear. Hoping we get better cards than the opponent. If someone is really lucky, they get (or have) the favorite dish in hand and can buy the customer with only 1 card. If you get lucky, you get lucky and win. I don't see much choice here. "Seize the bean" can be an upgrade if you want to play with this kind of gameplay. But even this better game, is not that good. B

[Rating: 2/10] Wow, this was just awful. Every single turn you have to go through customers comparing their icons to your icons. An absolute chore and exactly zero fun.
